newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-CHAMPIONS FRANCE WALK DAVIS CUP TIGHTROPE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHAMPIONS FRANCE WALK DAVIS CUP TIGHTROPE.

text.p: France's grip on the Davis Cup they won in extraordinary circumstances just nine weeks ago looked fatally weak on Friday as home advantage proved a vital weapon in the opening singles of several World Group first round ties.

The French trailed Australia 2-0 in Sydney after Patrick Rafter and Mark Woodforde downed Cedric Pioline and Arnaud Boetsch, Rafter squeezing past Pioline from two sets down, and must now rely on the world's best doubles partnership suffering an off-day on Saturday.
The celebrated duo of Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge will clinch the tie if they beat Guy Forget and Guillaume Raoux, and even French captain Yannick Noah is struggling to locate an escape route.

"Obviously it's not going to be easy because we're not playing just any doubles team," said Noah, whose team recovered from 2-0 down against Sweden to triumph in Malmo in December. "But we've been there before and we have to dig deep again and come back."
Australia, back in the World Group after two years' absence, opted to stage the tie on a grass court at White City and temperatures of 36 degrees Celsius also tested French resolve.

Pioline, ranked 26th in the world compared to Rafter's 64th place, found the heat increasingly draining in a contest which lasted four hours 15 minutes, but it was still a magnificent effort from the Australian who has been dogged by injuries and inconsistent form in the past two years.
"I knew he could win in five sets but that it would take a superhuman effort," Australian captain John Newcombe said.
Last year's beaten finalists Sweden could also face a testing weekend after Switzerland's Marc Rosset beat Magnus Larsson 13-11 in the fifth set of a marathon opening singles in Lulea.
Thomas Enqvist managed to level the tie with a 7-6 7-6 6-2 victory over Lorenzo Manta, but Sweden can reassure themselves that away wins seem likely to be at a premium this weekend.
Spain cruised to a 2-0 lead over Germany on clay in Mallorca, where local boy Carlos Moya continued his impressive recent form by crushing Marc Goellner 6-4 6-3 6-3.

Moya, beaten finalist in the Australian Open singles last month, was expertly backed up by Alberto Costa and Germany, champions in 1993, seem unlikely to enjoy the rest of their weekend on the holiday island.
Romania were also giving the Netherlands a hard time in Bucharest where Adrian Voinea and Andrei Pavel defeated Paul Haarhuis and Jan Siemerink to give the home country an unexpected 2-0 lead.

Italy opened up a comfortable 2-0 advantage over Mexico in spring-like conditions in Rome, but Leander Paes pulled India back into contention against the Czech Republic with a 6-2 6-3 6-7 6-3 victory over Jiri Novak in Pribram.
The United States had to call on all the experience of MaliVai Washington and Jim Courier to prevent the United States losing control in hostile conditions in Brazil.

Washington, called up to replace the injured Andre Agassi, lost the first set to Brazil's Gustavo Kuerten in Ribeirao Preto and had two set points against him in the tie-break at the end of the second.
But Washington saved both points, then went on to win the tie-break 8-6 and the match 3-6 7-6 7-6 6-3 in three hours and ten minutes, silencing the samba drums in a noisy 4,000 crowd.
Courier made it 2-0, but only after a three-hour 50 minute battle of wills with Fernando Meligeni during which fans were warned by the umpire for throwing cardboard on to the court.
The most sapping conditions worldwide, though, were probably in Durban where South Africa opened up a significant early lead over Russia before rain caused an early finish.

In high humidity accompanied by on-court temperatures of 41 degrees Celsius, South Africa's number two player Marcus Ondruska upset Russian number one Andrei Chesnokov 7-6 6-3 3-6 4-6 7-5 in a five-set marathon which left both players exhausted.

"I felt like dead meat on the court - the heat was terrible," Chesnokov said. "Only once before, in Singapore, have I experienced heat as bad. I don't think I was in good shape today and he played much better than me over the last three games."

In the second rubber of the day, world number eight Wayne Ferreira was locked at five-games all in his opening set against Russian number two Andre Cherkasov when persistent rain ended play for the day.
